t.E120.agn: In its 2015 re-evaluation EFSA confirmed the acceptable daily intake (ADI) of 2.5 mg/kg body weight as carminic acid (5 mg/kg as carmine) and did not find carminic acid to be genotoxic. Because insect proteins remaining from production may rarely cause allergic reactions, it recommended improving purification methods.
t.E120.body: There are no studies directly examining how carmine and carminic acid are processed in the body; indirect findings suggest that carmines are absorbed and distributed in the body.
t.E120.eff.0.t: Allergic reactions have rarely been reported due to insect proteins remaining from production
t.E120.eval: A red dye obtained from the cochineal insect (not vegan). Its halal acceptability varies according to religious authorities. Rare allergic reactions have been reported.
t.E120.prod: Obtained from the cochineal insect by extraction with water or alcohol.
t.E120.pw.0: It is not vegan because it is obtained from an insect.
t.E120.pw.1: It is of insect origin; many vegetarians do not consume this substance.
t.E120.reg.0: Re-evaluated; ADI 2.5 mg/kg as carminic acid.
t.E120.reg.1: In Türkiye, included in the Turkish Food Codex list of permitted additives.
t.E120.summary: A red colour obtained from the cochineal insect.
t.E120.what: Gives food a colour between red and pink.
